title: 1.4.0b2+ no longer calls dispose on InstrumentationManager

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: external extension issues
labels.description: an extension to SQLAlchemy may be producing a problem

body:
**Describe the bug**
I have a custom `InstrumentationManager` extending `sqlalchemy.ext.instrumentation.InstrumentationManager`.

`InstrumentationManager` uses `_default_class_manager` as the attribute where it stores the class manager instead of the default one `_sa_class_manager`.


**Expected behavior**
`sqlalchemy.orm.clear_mappers()` should remove the attribute `_default_class_manager` from the mapped class. So creating a new mapper afterwards is possible.

Until https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/5ec5b0a6c7b618bba7926e21f77be9557973860f#diff-5e3090555a0af448d2716136198d1b606fcbc5253df1065c04b4abaae1ac2e60L541 this was the case because `manager.dispose` delegated to `InstrumentationManager.dispose` which removes the attribute.

With the change in 1.4.0b2 `ClassManager` just tries to remove the attribute named `self.MANAGER_ATTR` (which in this case has the value of `'_sa_class_manager'`).
See https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/5ec5b0a6c7b618bba7926e21f77be9557973860f#diff-5e3090555a0af448d2716136198d1b606fcbc5253df1065c04b4abaae1ac2e60R357


**To Reproduce**

```py
from sqlalchemy.ext import instrumentation
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, Table, String, create_engine
import sqlalchemy.orm
import sqlalchemy.schema


metadata = sqlalchemy.schema.MetaData()
metadata.bind = create_engine('sqlite://')

table = Table(
    'my-table', metadata,
    Column('mytable_id', Integer, primary_key=True),
    Column('value', String(50)))
metadata.create_all()


class MyInstrumentation(instrumentation.InstrumentationManager):
    """The actual implementation does not seem to matter."""

    def dispose(self, class_):
        # workaround required for SQLAlchemy 1.3:
        # instrumentation.InstrumentationManager.dispose()
        # needs 3 arguments, but is called with only 2 arguments.
        # (Not called in SQLAlchemy 1.4)
        return super().dispose(class_, manager=None)

    # My current workaround for SQLAlchemy 1.4.x:
    # def manage(self, class_, manager):
    #     manager.MANAGER_ATTR = '_default_class_manager'
    #     super().manage(class_, manager)


instrumentation.instrumentation_finders.append(
    lambda cls: MyInstrumentation)


def extended_manager_of_class(cls):
    """Redirect to the attribute where the manager class is stored."""
    return cls.__dict__.get('_default_class_manager', None)

instrumentation._instrumentation_factory.manager_of_class = (
    extended_manager_of_class)


class MyTable:
    mytable_id = None
    value = None

mapper = sqlalchemy.orm.mapper(MyTable, table)

sqlalchemy.orm.clear_mappers()

mapper = sqlalchemy.orm.mapper(MyTable, table)

print('Success!')
```

**Error**

happens on the second call to `sqlalchemy.orm.mapper`: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "example.py", line 53, in <module>
    mapper = sqlalchemy.orm.mapper(MyTable, table)
  File "<string>", line 2, in mapper
  File "<string>", line 2, in __init__
  File ".../sqlalchemy/util/deprecations.py", line 298, in warned
    return fn(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../sqlalchemy/orm/mapper.py", line 683, in __init__
    self._configure_class_instrumentation()
  File ".../sqlalchemy/orm/mapper.py", line 1214, in _configure_class_instrumentation
    % self.class_
sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: Class '<class '__main__.MyTable'>' already has a primary mapper defined.
```

**Versions.**
 - OS: MacOS 10.15.7
 - Python: 3.7.10
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4.11
 - Database: any (not dependent on database)

**Additional context**

* Running the same example on the latest SQLAlchemy 1.3 prints 'Success' as there is no exception.
* I added my current workaround as a comment to the example. – Maybe this is not the way to go but it seems to work.

**Have a nice day!** 😀
